title: A Scoping Review of Adherence for Caregiver-Implemented Intervention Regimens for Individuals With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities
abstract: Interventions for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities often require long-term caregiver adherence. A scoping review method was used to search for peer-reviewed studies published between 2000 and 2024. Studies were screened for inclusion based on if they measured caregiver adherence to an intervention for a child diagnosed with an intellectual or developmental disability. The search yielded 125 articles. Of these, 26 articles met the inclusion criteria and were reviewed. Articles were more likely to include female caregivers of younger children. Most articles used quantitative correlational methodology. The most common adherence measurement tool was surveys. Most articles reported caregiver adherence levels; however, there was substantial variation in how adherence was reported across articles. Several variables related to the caregiver, child, caregiver training, and intervention were reported to influence adherence. Future researchers should directly evaluate the effects of reported variables on caregiver adherence and evaluate how modifying potential barriers impacts adherence.
